I am sixty years old and I have been farming in Quzhou all my life. I never went to school, but I know this land better than anyone. My husband passed away a few years back, so now it is me and my son, who comes home from the city factory when he can. We have about ten mu.

The wheat went in last October, same as every year. I plant improved wheat seed — Luyuan 502, the kind they sell at the county shop. It costs more than saving your own seed, but it gives me around one thousand jin per mu, so it is worth it. I have eight mu of wheat. I rotary-till the land before planting, and now in spring I will irrigate it three times — green-up, jointing, and grain-filling. I put down about two bags of compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea when the wheat starts growing fast. I learned this from my father and from watching my neighbors. If they do well, I do the same.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, there is no time to waste. We plant maize right away on seven mu of that same land. We use no-tillage planting — the machine puts the hybrid maize seed straight into the wheat stubble. There is no time to plough between crops, and everyone in our village does it this way now. The maize gets about one bag of compound fertilizer when we plant it, and I irrigate it twice if the rains do not come.

I also keep two mu for cotton. The cotton price was decent last year, and I need the cash income. But I am getting old and the spraying is hard work — fifteen times or more — so I cut it back from what I used to grow. My son helps with the heavy spraying when he is home.

I do not read books or use the internet. I decide by what I have seen work before, and by what the successful farmers in my village are doing.
